title: Arrested without his draft card in Missouri and sent to Camp Funston
summary: White tells of being jailed for lacking his registration card and being sent on to camp.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah, and when they asked for the card, there were about five of us in there who were supposed to be fellows of war age. And I didn't have my card in my pocket. The fact of it is I had gone to the circus that day in my shirt sleeve because we put on our band coats in the tent, under the tent. And well, where's your card? And they got right hostile with me, you know. They grabbed me. I said, it's down the privilege card. No, you won't go get anything, they said. We're going to take you on in. You were instructed to have that card on you. So they took me straight on to the jail. And then I got busy. Miles went and got my card, brought it to me. But by that time, the commissioners have all gone. So now I got to spend this night in there. And this is on a Saturday afternoon. Now this is Sunday and Miles is off. So Miles came to the jail and brought me my week's salary and some more money. I think he all totally gave me about $40. And he brought some clothes to me. And I said, well, I don't need any clothes because I'm going on to the Army. I know it. He brought my card to me. Well, when the commissioners came to sit in Sunday afternoon and Sheriff Dawes was the sheriff there in Nevada, Missouri. You see, they didn't take me up in Sedalia. Well, they took me where the regular United States commissioner's office was, and that was in Nevada, Missouri. They had different points for these places and states. And regardless of the fact that Sedalia was a much bigger city than Nevada, still they took me to Nevada. After I approved registration and everything, they were no longer hostile. They had a commissioner. Three commissioners came in on a Sunday afternoon on request of Sheriff Dawes. Sheriff Dawes said, well, I don't see what they want to keep you in here for. You approved registration. You got your card and everything. He says, I'm going to call them up down there. They're still in. So they made a special trip back there to jail and they sat in and said, well, what do you want to do? You didn't have that card on you. I said, I want to go to the service. I said, the fact of it is I had written Mr. Michael, Eugene Michael, my former teacher. I had written James Reese Europe because a lot of boys out of the Jenkins office was in his band, just a whole lot. In fact, the boy who killed James Reese Europe was a student of mine, Herbert Wright, but only, yeah, but I was just about a few months older than Herbert. Well, they sent me on to camp. I rode all that evening. No sheriff went there or anything. And all that night, I sidetracked on the road in a little town in Kansas, some place way down the border there, going to Camp Funston. That was in Kansas? No, this was in Missouri where I was in jail. But now they're sending me to camp. On this long trek to Camp Funston, you got to cut around through the corner of Missouri, cut around through the corner of Oklahoma and to Kansas, and then go up to Camp Funston, you see. You see, that's the way they— I don't remember where it was. It's time. Camp Funston is way up in the corner of Kansas. Where is it now?
I can't picture it. It's in Kansas, though.
Yeah, it's in Kansas, but it's not in central Kansas. You're almost over to the mountainous side. You're almost around to the Colorado corner.
Colorado or South Dakota. New Mexico.
